content.value: WAVE CLOSED (Review, 2026-07-16). blocks.text: The wish

content.value: W4 is the epic's endgame clause: commands become a Barkpark content type, so a repo pulls its scaffolding over ONE CONNECT, like Papers and Tasks. Five wish items: (1) a command schema registered plugin-side (register_schemas/1, plugin-declared is the law), storing the .scaffy source verbatim as the artifact plus label-spine metadata — title/description/weighted tags, CONCEPT/VARIANT/DOMAIN queryable; (2) idempotent seeding of the 7 corpus commands to guerrilla as command documents; (3) bp scaffy pull <concept>[/<variant>] (verb surface to be DECIDED honestly against the scaffy noun, incl. the north-star spelling bp add) fetching from the connected server, W2-validated BEFORE anything can run, written under scaffy/commands/ or run with --var passthrough; (4) catalog browse — bp scaffy ls --remote (concept × variant × domain table) and command documents readable in Studio (source as code, metadata visible, reuse existing surfaces); (5) showcase/masterplan papers gain a 'commands are served now' section and the epic's W4 criterion is stamped. Security/trust is a first-class DECIDE topic: a fetched command executes shell via ASSERT CMD — validate-first is necessary but not sufficient; consider opt-in LOCAL asserts or a confirmation gate listing the CMDs. Orchestration law (three strikes, D43): dependent slices NEVER dispatch in the same round as their unmerged deps.

blocks.text: Direction — what finished feels like

content.value: From any repo with bp connected: bp scaffy ls --remote shows the catalog — 7 commands as a concept × variant × domain table. bp scaffy pull add-block-type fetches the command document, runs the W2 validator over the fetched bytes BEFORE anything touches disk-as-runnable, writes it under scaffy/commands/ with provenance, and prints the exact shell lines (ASSERT CMDs) the command would execute. Running it then behaves exactly like a local command — same engine, same receipts, same byte-clean remove. Commands are real documents: readable in Studio with the source as a code rendering and the label spine (title, description, weighted tags, concept/variant/domain) visible and queryable.

Tentative leanings (Decide finalizes after two explore rounds): (a) Schema owner — a new lightweight scaffy plugin owning the command schema via register_schemas/1 — the house pattern, and poetic dogfood of add-plugin.scaffy. Riding an existing plugin (bulldocs/tasks) only if survey shows the new-plugin cost is real. (b) Source verbatim — ONE text field carries the .scaffy bytes; the file IS the truth, never a lossy block decomposition. Metadata fields sit beside it, derived at seed time from the parsed header — never hand-maintained twice. (c) Seeding — doc.create-or-replace keyed by a stable concept–variant id, driven from the repo corpus: repo scaffy/commands/ = the truth, server = distribution; the seed step is a one-way idempotent upsert (re-runnable, drift overwrites serverward). (d) Verb surface — bp scaffy pull + bp scaffy ls --remote are the honest core under the existing noun. bp add <concept> is the north-star spelling and stays on the table ONLY as a thin alias if survey shows a cheap, non-colliding dispatch path — never a second implementation. (e) Trust — pull NEVER auto-runs. Validate-first is mandatory (zero findings or the fetch is refused loudly, exit 5). Any run of a pulled command enumerates its CMD surface (ASSERT CMD lines) and requires explicit consent (--yes or interactive confirm); provenance (server, doc id, rev, source sha256) is recorded so drift is detectable. (f) Studio — reuse the generic document surfaces; a new LiveView only if the brief proves it one-block cheap.

Priorities: schema + seeding land FIRST (everything downstream needs live command documents); pull + trust gate second; catalog + Studio readability third; papers stamp last. Sequencing per D43 is non-negotiable: if the dispatcher cannot sequence rounds, dependent slices are filed as open tasks with AFTER-X-merges brief lines and the lead runs manual sequential rounds (4-for-4 in W3). Quality bar: the pull path must be as byte-honest as the engine — validated before runnable, refused loudly on findings, never executing unvalidated remote content.

blocks.text: Digest — survey synthesis (14 reports, 2026-07-16)

content.value: Established, with file:line evidence. (1) Schema home: a NEW lightweight scaffy plugin owns the command schema — bulldocs is the exemplar (register_schemas/1 reads priv/plugins/<name>/schemas/*.json, bulldocs.ex:141-158); Bootstrap.register_all_schemas/0 gives idempotent (name,dataset) upsert into the Default workspace/project for free (bootstrap.ex:45-101). add-plugin.scaffy scaffolds the 5-file skeleton but NOT the schema declaration — that is a small manual follow-up.

(2) Schema shape: source = ONE plain string field holding the verbatim .scaffy bytes; concept/variant/domain = plain strings; tags = hand-authored arrayOf(composite{tag,strength,rationale}) copied from paper.json — no reusable weighted-tags type exists anywhere. Visibility DEFAULT is "public" (schema_definition.ex:11, read directly at digest — this resolves a survey contradiction: the auth-connect-path report claimed private-default, wrong; schema-v2-modeling was right). Public visibility = tokenless anonymous reads via query_controller.ex:14 — genuinely one-connect, matching paper's precedent (the only public schema among live plugins).

(3) Header parity: the .scaffy header grammar already carries COMMAND/DESCRIPTION/LAST_UPDATED/DOMAIN/TAGS/CONCEPT/VARIANT/DIRECTION as first-class parsed fields with a closed keyset (parse.go:187,257) — metadata derives at seed time from Parse(), zero grammar work. TAGS parses as one joined string; the seeder splits it into the weighted-tags array. All 7 corpus files carry full headers; DOMAIN is uniformly "barkpark" today (real grammar, constant-valued corpus).

(4) Seeding: bp doc create-or-replace exists (createOrReplace mutation, capabilities.ex:807-827) BUT its manifest declares no --file flag while the generic help text advertises one — a real, narrow bug (one missing flag() line; doc.create and doc.mutate both have it) that blocks multi-line source payloads through that verb. Fork for Decide: fix the flag and use generic create-or-replace, vs a small bulldocs-style plugin ingest endpoint (upsert-by-slug, proven live by this epic's own showcase paper, D18/block_ops.ex:68-113). Stable id: domain--concept--variant (concept alone is non-unique — docs-card has add and remove variants).

(5) CLI seams: TestScaffyPureLocal is a raw byte-substring scan of scaffy_cmd.go ONLY (scaffy_cmd_test.go:773-782, bans the literal strings resolveContext/loadManifest, comments included) — pull/ls-remote MUST live in a new file (scaffy_remote_cmd.go pattern) dispatched from runScaffy's switch; paper_cmd.go:136 is the precedent for a builtin resolving its own context. A manifest verb models exactly one HTTP call (manifest.go:67-91, no local-action field) — pull's validate/consent/write logic can never be server-declared; the raw fetch rides the generic doc get/query commands. bp add collides with nothing but overloads an established sub-verb vocabulary — thin alias at most, never a second implementation.

(6) Catalog: zero new API surface — GET /v1/data/query/:dataset/:type with ?fields=+?order= serves the concept×variant×domain table; the CLI table renderer already handles the documents envelope and auto-picks columns (table.go:69-84,273-309). Known wart: repeated --filter silently degrades to last-value-wins (Plug flat params) — invisible at 7 docs, noted for Decide.

(7) Studio: every non-paper/sheet/graph type renders via the one generic studio_editor_shell; array/object fields already render a read-only monospace <pre> (field_inputs.ex:294-305 — live today for ticket messages). "text" renders a plain non-monospace textarea; no code/syntax field type exists. OPEN: readonly_json on a bare string may JSON-escape multi-line source into one quoted line — verifier proves this before the field type is locked.

(8) Trust: exactly ONE shell-exec call site in the engine (apply.go:719), reached only via Assert.Kind==AssertCmd; CMD text is var-substituted BEFORE exec (apply.go:699) — any consent enumeration must show SUBSTITUTED text, not raw source, or it lies. TIER ci asserts never execute locally. House conventions: --yes gate naming the flag, type-to-confirm for destructive ops, --dry-run checked before the gate. NO sandboxing exists anywhere (the connectors exec-isolation crux is open and deferred) — W4's trust model is gating + provenance, never isolation. Pull NEVER auto-runs.

(9) Provenance: .scaffy/ is hard-gitignored (.gitignore:82 — run receipts are deliberately ephemeral) — pull provenance must be a COMMITTED sidecar (scaffy/commands/<name>.provenance.json: server, doc id, rev, source sha256, fetched_at) and the pulled .scaffy file stays byte-identical to the served source (no in-band banner; sha256 stays a real trust anchor). Drift check = recompute local sha vs sidecar vs server rev, loud refusal on mismatch.

(10) Papers stamp: exact stale blocks identified — masterplan scf-053 (two W4-future bullets + one stale W3 bullet) with scf-055 as the voice template; showcase scs-056/057 ("What ships next") still narrates W2/W3 as future and contradicts its own scs-059 W3-amendment three blocks earlier. Checked-in scaffy/showcase/*.json payloads are byte-identical to the live papers — the D18 re-ingest recipe reproduces live state exactly; edit in place, re-POST.

(11) W3 residue: all 5 W3 PRs are MERGED (gh-verified #3743/#3745/#3748/#3754/#3755; ledger tasks done) and the engine was live-proven during survey (validate clean on 7/7, validate --repo anchors_ok:9, run --dry-run refuses bad vars exit 2 and writes zero bytes). The charter's W3 wave log claiming 4-of-5 stalled is STALE — Review owes the correction stamp. 8 backlog tasks open, none blocks W4 (two adjacencies: add-schema-type is a CORPUS command, NOT W4's doctype — do not conflate; elixir-local-gate-proof is load-bearing for slice 1's gate). No pre-filed W4 tasks — clean slate. Go builds need CC=/usr/bin/clang.

blocks.text: Verify — what the deep round proved (6 verifiers, 2026-07-16)

elixir-ground-proof: targeted single-file plugin mix test runs LOCALLY — media_test.exs → "3 tests, 0 failures" in 9.0s wall; slice gates can be local mix test lines, refuting the backlog worry (task closed at Decide). createOrReplace is green on main (pusher+backfill 42 tests, mutate_controller 12 tests, 0 failures). POST /v1/data/mutate performs ZERO schema-field validation: validate_document has exactly two callers repo-wide, both UI (forms.ex:242, studio doc.ex:21) — so the seeding fork is NOT differentiated by validation; the seeder owns correctness. content is jsonb with no practical cap; title is varchar(255) — the source must ride in content, never title.

create-or-replace-file-repro: the --file gap is REAL at runtime, not a manifest-reading artifact — `bp doc create-or-replace paper --file x.json --dry-run` fails exit 2 with "bp: unknown flag --file for doc create-or-replace" BEFORE any network call, because capabilities.ex:807-829 declares only flag("set") while the generic Writes help line (usage.go:144-151) advertises --file for every write verb. doc.create (:796) and doc.mutate (:710) are working controls; create-if-not-exists carries the identical gap. One-line-class fix — does not justify forking to a bespoke ingest endpoint.

studio-source-rendering: readonly_json on a bare multi-line .scaffy source emits a ONE-LINE JSON-escaped blob (proof: "# add-block-type v1\nCONCEPT add-block-type…" — every newline \n, every quote \\") — the array/object clause is disqualified for the source field. type "text" is readable but EDITABLE + form-submitted (a Studio save silently diverges server from repo). The winning shape: a new ~9-line FieldInputs clause for a fresh field type — read-only monospace <pre>, RAW value, NO form input (absent from params ⇒ Classic save preserves bytes byte-identical, forms.ex:168-181 precedent).

dry-run-as-consent-surface: `bp scaffy run --dry-run` ALREADY enumerates the substituted CMD surface — RunReport.Asserts[] carries the real var-woven shell text (proof: "echo checking widget && grep -q widget probe_widget.txt", status would-run), TIER ci CMDs come back status deferred ("TIER ci — deferred to the PR, never run locally"), and dry-run writes NOTHING. The consent gate is a REUSE, not an invention. Nuances that bind the design: injection commands abort at the op stage on anchor mismatch (distinct UX path, no CMD list); ValidateFile takes bytes (pre-write gate for fetched content); the substituter is unexported — enumeration is reachable ONLY through Run's dry-run; only 3 of 7 corpus commands have LOCAL would-run CMDs (4 are ci-only — say "no local commands run" honestly).

Live on guerrilla: tokenless GET of a public type returns 200 with documents; a private type 404s existence-hiding ("document not found") — visibility:"public" on the command schema IS the one-connect story. bp doc query --fields/--order renders a correctly projected+sorted table (zero new API for the catalog); caveat: columns empty across the whole page are dropped from the header (backlogged).

content.value: From any repo with bp connected: bp scaffy ls --remote shows the catalog — 7 commands as a concept × variant × domain table. bp scaffy pull add-block-type fetches the command document, runs the W2 validator over the fetched bytes BEFORE anything touches disk-as-runnable, writes it under scaffy/commands/ with provenance, and prints the exact shell lines (ASSERT CMDs) the command would execute. Commands are real documents: readable in Studio with the source as a code rendering and the label spine (title, description, weighted tags, concept/variant/domain) visible and queryable.

Tentative leanings (Decide finalizes after two explore rounds): (a) Schema owner — a new lightweight scaffy plugin owning the command schema via register_schemas/1 — the house pattern, and poetic dogfood of add-plugin.scaffy. Riding an existing plugin (bulldocs/tasks) only if survey shows the new-plugin cost is real. (b) Source verbatim — ONE text field carries the .scaffy bytes; the file IS the truth, never a lossy block decomposition. Metadata fields sit beside it, derived at seed time from the parsed header — never hand-maintained twice. (c) Seeding — doc.create-or-replace keyed by a stable concept–variant id, driven from the repo corpus: repo scaffy/commands/ = the truth, server = distribution; the seed step is a one-way idempotent upsert (re-runnable, drift overwrites serverward). Any run of a pulled command enumerates its CMD surface (ASSERT CMD lines) and requires explicit consent (--yes or interactive confirm); provenance (server, doc id, rev, source sha256) is recorded so drift is detectable. (f) Studio — reuse the generic document surfaces; a new LiveView only if the brief proves it one-block cheap.

Scaffy · Wave 4 · Commands as Content

Scaffy W4 — Commands as Content: the wave story

WAVE CLOSED (Review, 2026-07-16). Round 1 built and reviewed — 3 of 5 slices ready to merge (branches named in the debrief below); rounds 2–3 (seed-corpus, live-proof+papers-stamp) stopped honestly on the D53 sequencing guard and re-dispatch after the merges. Earlier phase beacons below ("in flight", "dispatching") are historical — the debrief at the end is the wave's outcome.

The wish

W4 is the epic's endgame clause: commands become a Barkpark content type, so a repo pulls its scaffolding over ONE CONNECT, like Papers and Tasks. Five wish items: (1) a command schema registered plugin-side (register_schemas/1, plugin-declared is the law), storing the .scaffy source verbatim as the artifact plus label-spine metadata — title/description/weighted tags, CONCEPT/VARIANT/DOMAIN queryable; (2) idempotent seeding of the 7 corpus commands to guerrilla as command documents; (3) bp scaffy pull <concept>[/<variant>] (verb surface to be DECIDED honestly against the scaffy noun, incl. the north-star spelling bp add) fetching from the connected server, W2-validated BEFORE anything can run, written under scaffy/commands/ or run with --var passthrough; (4) catalog browse — bp scaffy ls --remote (concept × variant × domain table) and command documents readable in Studio (source as code, metadata visible, reuse existing surfaces); (5) showcase/masterplan papers gain a 'commands are served now' section and the epic's W4 criterion is stamped. Security/trust is a first-class DECIDE topic: a fetched command executes shell via ASSERT CMD — validate-first is necessary but not sufficient; consider opt-in LOCAL asserts or a confirmation gate listing the CMDs. Orchestration law (three strikes, D43): dependent slices NEVER dispatch in the same round as their unmerged deps.

Where the epic stands

W1–W3 are ALL merged and live: the 7-command corpus + README + showcase paper (W1, #3608–#3615), the grammar law + internal/scaffy validator + bp scaffy validate/fmt + corpus conformance (W2, #3657–#3664), and the full engine — subst/apply/fat receipts (#3743), receipt-replay remove (#3745), bp scaffy run/remove CLI (#3748), validate --repo (#3754), showcase rev-3 with real transcripts (#3755). The epic task carries north-star evidence: add-block-type run (2 created + 6 injected, vitest 255/255) → all-skip rerun → remove → git diff --stat EMPTY; REANCHOR ×2 oban accretes forward and removes byte-clean. Ledger correction owed: the charter's W3 wave log still reads '1 of 5 slices, 4 stalled' — stale; the sequenced re-dispatch completed and every W3 slice is done. Review stamps the correction. Open backlog riding into W4 triage: js-assert-sweep, oban-cron-guard-gap, pnpm-assert-overbroad, docs-anchors-nm-prune, api-route-parity, add-schema-type, elixir-local-gate-proof, anchors-omx-exclusion.

Direction — what finished feels like

From any repo with bp connected: bp scaffy ls --remote shows the catalog — 7 commands as a concept × variant × domain table. bp scaffy pull add-block-type fetches the command document, runs the W2 validator over the fetched bytes BEFORE anything touches disk-as-runnable, writes it under scaffy/commands/ with provenance, and prints the exact shell lines (ASSERT CMDs) the command would execute. Running it then behaves exactly like a local command — same engine, same receipts, same byte-clean remove. Commands are real documents: readable in Studio with the source as a code rendering and the label spine (title, description, weighted tags, concept/variant/domain) visible and queryable.

Tentative leanings (Decide finalizes after two explore rounds): (a) Schema owner — a new lightweight scaffy plugin owning the command schema via register_schemas/1 — the house pattern, and poetic dogfood of add-plugin.scaffy. Riding an existing plugin (bulldocs/tasks) only if survey shows the new-plugin cost is real. (b) Source verbatim — ONE text field carries the .scaffy bytes; the file IS the truth, never a lossy block decomposition. Metadata fields sit beside it, derived at seed time from the parsed header — never hand-maintained twice. (c) Seeding — doc.create-or-replace keyed by a stable concept–variant id, driven from the repo corpus: repo scaffy/commands/ = the truth, server = distribution; the seed step is a one-way idempotent upsert (re-runnable, drift overwrites serverward). (d) Verb surface — bp scaffy pull + bp scaffy ls --remote are the honest core under the existing noun. bp add <concept> is the north-star spelling and stays on the table ONLY as a thin alias if survey shows a cheap, non-colliding dispatch path — never a second implementation. (e) Trust — pull NEVER auto-runs. Validate-first is mandatory (zero findings or the fetch is refused loudly, exit 5). Any run of a pulled command enumerates its CMD surface (ASSERT CMD lines) and requires explicit consent (--yes or interactive confirm); provenance (server, doc id, rev, source sha256) is recorded so drift is detectable. (f) Studio — reuse the generic document surfaces; a new LiveView only if the brief proves it one-block cheap.

Priorities: schema + seeding land FIRST (everything downstream needs live command documents); pull + trust gate second; catalog + Studio readability third; papers stamp last. Sequencing per D43 is non-negotiable: if the dispatcher cannot sequence rounds, dependent slices are filed as open tasks with AFTER-X-merges brief lines and the lead runs manual sequential rounds (4-for-4 in W3). Quality bar: the pull path must be as byte-honest as the engine — validated before runnable, refused loudly on findings, never executing unvalidated remote content.

Survey plan — 14 scouts

plugin-schema-owner — Where should the command schema live? Read api/CLAUDE.md's doc-type law + live register_schemas/1 exemplars (tasks, tickets, bulldocs plugins; plugin.json + schemas/ dir). Report exactly what files a plugin-declared command type needs, and whether a NEW scaffy plugin vs riding an existing plugin is house-consistent. Why: This is slice 1's whole shape — plugin-declared is the law; the owner decision cascades into every other slice.

schema-v2-modeling — docs/contracts/schema-v2.md: which field types exist; how to model source as one text field, concept/variant/domain as queryable fields, and the weighted-tags shape papers use (tags[{tag,strength,rationale}]) — schema-reusable? What does visibility public vs private mean for anonymous reads? Why: Field design for the command schema; visibility decides whether pull needs a token.

seeding-mechanism — Prior art for idempotent seeding: bp doc create-or-replace (exists — confirm semantics), the bulldocs papers upsert-by-slug ingest, Bootstrap.register_all_schemas, seeds.exs. Any repo-files-to-server sync precedent? Recommend the mechanism for '7 corpus commands to guerrilla, repo = truth'. Why: Wish item 2 is an explicit DECIDE (create-or-replace vs seeder); the answer sets the seed slice's size.

cli-pure-local-guard — internal/cli/scaffy_cmd.go + TestScaffyPureLocal: the guard's exact mechanics (raw substring scan — D40 trap), and how server-talking verbs acquire context (resolveContext/loadManifest call sites in doc/task verbs). Can pull / ls --remote live in scaffy_cmd.go at all, or does the guard force a new file or a different noun? Why: Decides the CLI architecture — the purity guard could red the whole slice if ignored.

verb-surface-prior-art — Map how bp fetches documents today (bp doc get/query paths, task verbs), how the builtin switch + completionNouns handle new nouns/verbs, and whether any precedent exists for a top-level alias like bp add. Why: Feeds the pull-vs-add DECIDE with facts instead of taste.

query-catalog-shape — What listing/filtering does the read API give us: /v1/data/query with field filters/projections, bp doc ls/query capabilities. Sketch the exact call behind bp scaffy ls --remote returning concept × variant × domain. Why: The catalog slice should be a projection over existing query power, not new API.

studio-command-rendering — How does Studio render a non-paper document type today (task, ticket): generic detail view? Can a long text field render monospace/code without a new LiveView? Name the cheapest path to 'source readable in Studio'. Why: Wish item 4 caps Studio work at reuse-unless-proven-cheap; this survey prices it.

trust-precedents — Search bp papers/tasks + the repo for remote-execution trust precedents (connectors exec-isolation, bp mcp serve curation, studio console gating) and CLI confirmation-gate precedents (--yes write global). Enumerate what internal/scaffy's AST exposes to list a command's ASSERT CMD strings pre-run. Why: The trust model is a first-class DECIDE; precedents keep it house-consistent and the AST answer prices the CMD-listing gate.

provenance-and-drift — Receipts already record command source sha256 (D35). Where should pulled-command provenance live (receipt, header comment, sidecar)? What happens today when a scaffy/commands/ file differs from the server copy — does validate --repo or anything else notice? Why: Two sources of truth is the standing risk; the truth law must be pinned at Decide.

header-metadata-parity — The .scaffy header grammar as parsed (ast.go/parse.go): which fields exist (NAME/TITLE/VARIANT/DIRECTION/TAGS/…)? Is DOMAIN a real field, derivable from TAGS/GROUP, or new grammar? Map header fields to the proposed schema fields. Why: Decides whether W4 touches the grammar at all — avoid if derivable; grammar changes drag validator + corpus + fixtures.

auth-connect-path — What 'one connect' means concretely: ~/.config/barkpark context resolution, bp login, token flow; can anonymous pull work if the schema is public? Which dataset do papers/tasks live in on guerrilla and where would command docs go (tenancy contract)? Why: Pull UX + the seeding target dataset both hang on this.

papers-stamp-scope — Current masterplan (/papers/scaffy-commands-as-content) + showcase (rev 3): which blocks claim 'Wave 4 will…'; where does the 'commands are served now' section go; confirm the checked-in payload path (scaffy/showcase/) + re-ingest recipe still work. Why: Wish item 5 — scoping it now keeps the papers slice small and last.

capabilities-manifest-verbs — How plugin cli_commands/0 verbs surface through GET /v1/capabilities into bp: could scaffy pull be a server-declared manifest verb (dogfooding add-cli-verb), and what can manifest verbs NOT do (local file writes, local validation hooks)? Why: Kills or confirms a tempting architecture before anyone builds it.

wave3-residue — Verify the ledger: confirm every W3 slice merged and bp scaffy run/remove/validate --repo behave on main today (--help + a --dry-run probe); list open scaffy backlog tasks W4 should absorb, sequence, or explicitly ignore; confirm the charter's stale W3 wave log needs a correction stamp. Why: Reconcile before building — the charter contradicts the ledger and the wave must start from truth.

Wave protocol

This paper is the wave's living story. Digest appends the survey digest + the verify-fleet plan before verifiers fly; Decide appends D-numbered decisions + the slice table (task ids named here, wave_paper stamped on every slice task) before builders fly; Review closes the story as the debrief and stamps the epic's W4 criterion. Epic task: bp-scaffy-epic (flat wave_status + wave_paper point here). Charter: .claude/workflows/bp-scaffy-charter.md.

Digest — survey synthesis (14 reports, 2026-07-16)

Established, with file:line evidence. (1) Schema home: a NEW lightweight scaffy plugin owns the command schema — bulldocs is the exemplar (register_schemas/1 reads priv/plugins/<name>/schemas/*.json, bulldocs.ex:141-158); Bootstrap.register_all_schemas/0 gives idempotent (name,dataset) upsert into the Default workspace/project for free (bootstrap.ex:45-101). add-plugin.scaffy scaffolds the 5-file skeleton but NOT the schema declaration — that is a small manual follow-up.

(2) Schema shape: source = ONE plain string field holding the verbatim .scaffy bytes; concept/variant/domain = plain strings; tags = hand-authored arrayOf(composite{tag,strength,rationale}) copied from paper.json — no reusable weighted-tags type exists anywhere. Visibility DEFAULT is "public" (schema_definition.ex:11, read directly at digest — this resolves a survey contradiction: the auth-connect-path report claimed private-default, wrong; schema-v2-modeling was right). Public visibility = tokenless anonymous reads via query_controller.ex:14 — genuinely one-connect, matching paper's precedent (the only public schema among live plugins).

(3) Header parity: the .scaffy header grammar already carries COMMAND/DESCRIPTION/LAST_UPDATED/DOMAIN/TAGS/CONCEPT/VARIANT/DIRECTION as first-class parsed fields with a closed keyset (parse.go:187,257) — metadata derives at seed time from Parse(), zero grammar work. TAGS parses as one joined string; the seeder splits it into the weighted-tags array. All 7 corpus files carry full headers; DOMAIN is uniformly "barkpark" today (real grammar, constant-valued corpus).

(4) Seeding: bp doc create-or-replace exists (createOrReplace mutation, capabilities.ex:807-827) BUT its manifest declares no --file flag while the generic help text advertises one — a real, narrow bug (one missing flag() line; doc.create and doc.mutate both have it) that blocks multi-line source payloads through that verb. Fork for Decide: fix the flag and use generic create-or-replace, vs a small bulldocs-style plugin ingest endpoint (upsert-by-slug, proven live by this epic's own showcase paper, D18/block_ops.ex:68-113). Stable id: domain--concept--variant (concept alone is non-unique — docs-card has add and remove variants).

(5) CLI seams: TestScaffyPureLocal is a raw byte-substring scan of scaffy_cmd.go ONLY (scaffy_cmd_test.go:773-782, bans the literal strings resolveContext/loadManifest, comments included) — pull/ls-remote MUST live in a new file (scaffy_remote_cmd.go pattern) dispatched from runScaffy's switch; paper_cmd.go:136 is the precedent for a builtin resolving its own context. A manifest verb models exactly one HTTP call (manifest.go:67-91, no local-action field) — pull's validate/consent/write logic can never be server-declared; the raw fetch rides the generic doc get/query commands. bp add collides with nothing but overloads an established sub-verb vocabulary — thin alias at most, never a second implementation.

(6) Catalog: zero new API surface — GET /v1/data/query/:dataset/:type with ?fields=+?order= serves the concept×variant×domain table; the CLI table renderer already handles the documents envelope and auto-picks columns (table.go:69-84,273-309). Known wart: repeated --filter silently degrades to last-value-wins (Plug flat params) — invisible at 7 docs, noted for Decide.

(7) Studio: every non-paper/sheet/graph type renders via the one generic studio_editor_shell; array/object fields already render a read-only monospace <pre> (field_inputs.ex:294-305 — live today for ticket messages). "text" renders a plain non-monospace textarea; no code/syntax field type exists. OPEN: readonly_json on a bare string may JSON-escape multi-line source into one quoted line — verifier proves this before the field type is locked.

(8) Trust: exactly ONE shell-exec call site in the engine (apply.go:719), reached only via Assert.Kind==AssertCmd; CMD text is var-substituted BEFORE exec (apply.go:699) — any consent enumeration must show SUBSTITUTED text, not raw source, or it lies. TIER ci asserts never execute locally. House conventions: --yes gate naming the flag, type-to-confirm for destructive ops, --dry-run checked before the gate. NO sandboxing exists anywhere (the connectors exec-isolation crux is open and deferred) — W4's trust model is gating + provenance, never isolation. Pull NEVER auto-runs.

(9) Provenance: .scaffy/ is hard-gitignored (.gitignore:82 — run receipts are deliberately ephemeral) — pull provenance must be a COMMITTED sidecar (scaffy/commands/<name>.provenance.json: server, doc id, rev, source sha256, fetched_at) and the pulled .scaffy file stays byte-identical to the served source (no in-band banner; sha256 stays a real trust anchor). Drift check = recompute local sha vs sidecar vs server rev, loud refusal on mismatch.

(10) Papers stamp: exact stale blocks identified — masterplan scf-053 (two W4-future bullets + one stale W3 bullet) with scf-055 as the voice template; showcase scs-056/057 ("What ships next") still narrates W2/W3 as future and contradicts its own scs-059 W3-amendment three blocks earlier. Scaffy · Wave 4 · Commands as Content

Scaffy W4 — Commands as Content: the wave story

WAVE CLOSED (Review, 2026-07-16). Round 1 built and reviewed — 3 of 5 slices ready to merge (branches named in the debrief below); rounds 2–3 (seed-corpus, live-proof+papers-stamp) stopped honestly on the D53 sequencing guard and re-dispatch after the merges. Earlier phase beacons below ("in flight", "dispatching") are historical — the debrief at the end is the wave's outcome.

The wish

W4 is the epic's endgame clause: commands become a Barkpark content type, so a repo pulls its scaffolding over ONE CONNECT, like Papers and Tasks. Five wish items: (1) a command schema registered plugin-side (register_schemas/1, plugin-declared is the law), storing the .scaffy source verbatim as the artifact plus label-spine metadata — title/description/weighted tags, CONCEPT/VARIANT/DOMAIN queryable; (2) idempotent seeding of the 7 corpus commands to guerrilla as command documents; (3) bp scaffy pull <concept>[/<variant>] (verb surface to be DECIDED honestly against the scaffy noun, incl. the north-star spelling bp add) fetching from the connected server, W2-validated BEFORE anything can run, written under scaffy/commands/ or run with --var passthrough; (4) catalog browse — bp scaffy ls --remote (concept × variant × domain table) and command documents readable in Studio (source as code, metadata visible, reuse existing surfaces); (5) showcase/masterplan papers gain a 'commands are served now' section and the epic's W4 criterion is stamped. Security/trust is a first-class DECIDE topic: a fetched command executes shell via ASSERT CMD — validate-first is necessary but not sufficient; consider opt-in LOCAL asserts or a confirmation gate listing the CMDs. Orchestration law (three strikes, D43): dependent slices NEVER dispatch in the same round as their unmerged deps.

Where the epic stands

W1–W3 are ALL merged and live: the 7-command corpus + README + showcase paper (W1, #3608–#3615), the grammar law + internal/scaffy validator + bp scaffy validate/fmt + corpus conformance (W2, #3657–#3664), and the full engine — subst/apply/fat receipts (#3743), receipt-replay remove (#3745), bp scaffy run/remove CLI (#3748), validate --repo (#3754), showcase rev-3 with real transcripts (#3755). The epic task carries north-star evidence: add-block-type run (2 created + 6 injected, vitest 255/255) → all-skip rerun → remove → git diff --stat EMPTY; REANCHOR ×2 oban accretes forward and removes byte-clean. Ledger correction owed: the charter's W3 wave log still reads '1 of 5 slices, 4 stalled' — stale; the sequenced re-dispatch completed and every W3 slice is done. Review stamps the correction. Open backlog riding into W4 triage: js-assert-sweep, oban-cron-guard-gap, pnpm-assert-overbroad, docs-anchors-nm-prune, api-route-parity, add-schema-type, elixir-local-gate-proof, anchors-omx-exclusion.

Direction — what finished feels like

From any repo with bp connected: bp scaffy ls --remote shows the catalog — 7 commands as a concept × variant × domain table. bp scaffy pull add-block-type fetches the command document, runs the W2 validator over the fetched bytes BEFORE anything touches disk-as-runnable, writes it under scaffy/commands/ with provenance, and prints the exact shell lines (ASSERT CMDs) the command would execute. Running it then behaves exactly like a local command — same engine, same receipts, same byte-clean remove. Commands are real documents: readable in Studio with the source as a code rendering and the label spine (title, description, weighted tags, concept/variant/domain) visible and queryable.

Tentative leanings (Decide finalizes after two explore rounds): (a) Schema owner — a new lightweight scaffy plugin owning the command schema via register_schemas/1 — the house pattern, and poetic dogfood of add-plugin.scaffy. Riding an existing plugin (bulldocs/tasks) only if survey shows the new-plugin cost is real. (b) Source verbatim — ONE text field carries the .scaffy bytes; the file IS the truth, never a lossy block decomposition. Metadata fields sit beside it, derived at seed time from the parsed header — never hand-maintained twice. (c) Seeding — doc.create-or-replace keyed by a stable concept–variant id, driven from the repo corpus: repo scaffy/commands/ = the truth, server = distribution; the seed step is a one-way idempotent upsert (re-runnable, drift overwrites serverward). (d) Verb surface — bp scaffy pull + bp scaffy ls --remote are the honest core under the existing noun. bp add <concept> is the north-star spelling and stays on the table ONLY as a thin alias if survey shows a cheap, non-colliding dispatch path — never a second implementation. (e) Trust — pull NEVER auto-runs. Validate-first is mandatory (zero findings or the fetch is refused loudly, exit 5). Any run of a pulled command enumerates its CMD surface (ASSERT CMD lines) and requires explicit consent (--yes or interactive confirm); provenance (server, doc id, rev, source sha256) is recorded so drift is detectable. (f) Studio — reuse the generic document surfaces; a new LiveView only if the brief proves it one-block cheap.

Priorities: schema + seeding land FIRST (everything downstream needs live command documents); pull + trust gate second; catalog + Studio readability third; papers stamp last. Sequencing per D43 is non-negotiable: if the dispatcher cannot sequence rounds, dependent slices are filed as open tasks with AFTER-X-merges brief lines and the lead runs manual sequential rounds (4-for-4 in W3). Quality bar: the pull path must be as byte-honest as the engine — validated before runnable, refused loudly on findings, never executing unvalidated remote content.

Survey plan — 14 scouts

plugin-schema-owner — Where should the command schema live? Read api/CLAUDE.md's doc-type law + live register_schemas/1 exemplars (tasks, tickets, bulldocs plugins; plugin.json + schemas/ dir). Report exactly what files a plugin-declared command type needs, and whether a NEW scaffy plugin vs riding an existing plugin is house-consistent. Why: This is slice 1's whole shape — plugin-declared is the law; the owner decision cascades into every other slice.

schema-v2-modeling — docs/contracts/schema-v2.md: which field types exist; how to model source as one text field, concept/variant/domain as queryable fields, and the weighted-tags shape papers use (tags[{tag,strength,rationale}]) — schema-reusable? What does visibility public vs private mean for anonymous reads? Why: Field design for the command schema; visibility decides whether pull needs a token.

seeding-mechanism — Prior art for idempotent seeding: bp doc create-or-replace (exists — confirm semantics), the bulldocs papers upsert-by-slug ingest, Bootstrap.register_all_schemas, seeds.exs. Any repo-files-to-server sync precedent? Recommend the mechanism for '7 corpus commands to guerrilla, repo = truth'. Why: Wish item 2 is an explicit DECIDE (create-or-replace vs seeder); the answer sets the seed slice's size.

cli-pure-local-guard — internal/cli/scaffy_cmd.go + TestScaffyPureLocal: the guard's exact mechanics (raw substring scan — D40 trap), and how server-talking verbs acquire context (resolveContext/loadManifest call sites in doc/task verbs). Can pull / ls --remote live in scaffy_cmd.go at all, or does the guard force a new file or a different noun? Why: Decides the CLI architecture — the purity guard could red the whole slice if ignored.

verb-surface-prior-art — Map how bp fetches documents today (bp doc get/query paths, task verbs), how the builtin switch + completionNouns handle new nouns/verbs, and whether any precedent exists for a top-level alias like bp add. Why: Feeds the pull-vs-add DECIDE with facts instead of taste.

query-catalog-shape — What listing/filtering does the read API give us: /v1/data/query with field filters/projections, bp doc ls/query capabilities. Sketch the exact call behind bp scaffy ls --remote returning concept × variant × domain. Why: The catalog slice should be a projection over existing query power, not new API.

studio-command-rendering — How does Studio render a non-paper document type today (task, ticket): generic detail view? Can a long text field render monospace/code without a new LiveView? Name the cheapest path to 'source readable in Studio'. Why: Wish item 4 caps Studio work at reuse-unless-proven-cheap; this survey prices it.

trust-precedents — Search bp papers/tasks + the repo for remote-execution trust precedents (connectors exec-isolation, bp mcp serve curation, studio console gating) and CLI confirmation-gate precedents (--yes write global). Enumerate what internal/scaffy's AST exposes to list a command's ASSERT CMD strings pre-run. Why: The trust model is a first-class DECIDE; precedents keep it house-consistent and the AST answer prices the CMD-listing gate.

What happens today when a scaffy/commands/ file differs from the server copy — does validate --repo or anything else notice? Why: Two sources of truth is the standing risk; the truth law must be pinned at Decide.

Is DOMAIN a real field, derivable from TAGS/GROUP, or new grammar? Map header fields to the proposed schema fields. Why: Decides whether W4 touches the grammar at all — avoid if derivable; grammar changes drag validator + corpus + fixtures.

Which dataset do papers/tasks live in on guerrilla and where would command docs go (tenancy contract)? Why: Pull UX + the seeding target dataset both hang on this.

Why: Wish item 5 — scoping it now keeps the papers slice small and last.

Why: Kills or confirms a tempting architecture before anyone builds it.

Why: Reconcile before building — the charter contradicts the ledger and the wave must start from truth.

Wave protocol

This paper is the wave's living story. Digest appends the survey digest + the verify-fleet plan before verifiers fly; Decide appends D-numbered decisions + the slice table (task ids named here, wave_paper stamped on every slice task) before builders fly; Review closes the story as the debrief and stamps the epic's W4 criterion. Epic task: bp-scaffy-epic (flat wave_status + wave_paper point here). Charter: .claude/workflows/bp-scaffy-charter.md.

Digest — survey synthesis (14 reports, 2026-07-16)

Established, with file:line evidence. (1) Schema home: a NEW lightweight scaffy plugin owns the command schema — bulldocs is the exemplar (register_schemas/1 reads priv/plugins/<name>/schemas/*.json, bulldocs.ex:141-158); Bootstrap.register_all_schemas/0 gives idempotent (name,dataset) upsert into the Default workspace/project for free (bootstrap.ex:45-101). add-plugin.scaffy scaffolds the 5-file skeleton but NOT the schema declaration — that is a small manual follow-up.

(2) Schema shape: source = ONE plain string field holding the verbatim .scaffy bytes; concept/variant/domain = plain strings; tags = hand-authored arrayOf(composite{tag,strength,rationale}) copied from paper.json — no reusable weighted-tags type exists anywhere. Visibility DEFAULT is "public" (schema_definition.ex:11, read directly at digest — this resolves a survey contradiction: the auth-connect-path report claimed private-default, wrong; schema-v2-modeling was right). Public visibility = tokenless anonymous reads via query_controller.ex:14 — genuinely one-connect, matching paper's precedent (the only public schema among live plugins).

(3) Header parity: the .scaffy header grammar already carries COMMAND/DESCRIPTION/LAST_UPDATED/DOMAIN/TAGS/CONCEPT/VARIANT/DIRECTION as first-class parsed fields with a closed keyset (parse.go:187,257) — metadata derives at seed time from Parse(), zero grammar work. TAGS parses as one joined string; the seeder splits it into the weighted-tags array. All 7 corpus files carry full headers; DOMAIN is uniformly "barkpark" today (real grammar, constant-valued corpus).

(4) Seeding: bp doc create-or-replace exists (createOrReplace mutation, capabilities.ex:807-827) BUT its manifest declares no --file flag while the generic help text advertises one — a real, narrow bug (one missing flag() line; doc.create and doc.mutate both have it) that blocks multi-line source payloads through that verb. Fork for Decide: fix the flag and use generic create-or-replace, vs a small bulldocs-style plugin ingest endpoint (upsert-by-slug, proven live by this epic's own showcase paper, D18/block_ops.ex:68-113). Stable id: domain--concept--variant (concept alone is non-unique — docs-card has add and remove variants).

(5) CLI seams: TestScaffyPureLocal is a raw byte-substring scan of scaffy_cmd.go ONLY (scaffy_cmd_test.go:773-782, bans the literal strings resolveContext/loadManifest, comments included) — pull/ls-remote MUST live in a new file (scaffy_remote_cmd.go pattern) dispatched from runScaffy's switch; paper_cmd.go:136 is the precedent for a builtin resolving its own context. A manifest verb models exactly one HTTP call (manifest.go:67-91, no local-action field) — pull's validate/consent/write logic can never be server-declared; the raw fetch rides the generic doc get/query commands. bp add collides with nothing but overloads an established sub-verb vocabulary — thin alias at most, never a second implementation.

(6) Catalog: zero new API surface — GET /v1/data/query/:dataset/:type with ?fields=+?order= serves the concept×variant×domain table; the CLI table renderer already handles the documents envelope and auto-picks columns (table.go:69-84,273-309). Known wart: repeated --filter silently degrades to last-value-wins (Plug flat params) — invisible at 7 docs, noted for Decide.

(7) Studio: every non-paper/sheet/graph type renders via the one generic studio_editor_shell; array/object fields already render a read-only monospace <pre> (field_inputs.ex:294-305 — live today for ticket messages). "text" renders a plain non-monospace textarea; no code/syntax field type exists. OPEN: readonly_json on a bare string may JSON-escape multi-line source into one quoted line — verifier proves this before the field type is locked.

(8) Trust: exactly ONE shell-exec call site in the engine (apply.go:719), reached only via Assert.Kind==AssertCmd; CMD text is var-substituted BEFORE exec (apply.go:699) — any consent enumeration must show SUBSTITUTED text, not raw source, or it lies. TIER ci asserts never execute locally. House conventions: --yes gate naming the flag, type-to-confirm for destructive ops, --dry-run checked before the gate. NO sandboxing exists anywhere (the connectors exec-isolation crux is open and deferred) — W4's trust model is gating + provenance, never isolation. Pull NEVER auto-runs.

(9) Provenance: .scaffy/ is hard-gitignored (.gitignore:82 — run receipts are deliberately ephemeral) — pull provenance must be a COMMITTED sidecar (scaffy/commands/<name>.provenance.json: server, doc id, rev, source sha256, fetched_at) and the pulled .scaffy file stays byte-identical to the served source (no in-band banner; sha256 stays a real trust anchor). Drift check = recompute local sha vs sidecar vs server rev, loud refusal on mismatch.

(10) Papers stamp: exact stale blocks identified — masterplan scf-053 (two W4-future bullets + one stale W3 bullet) with scf-055 as the voice template; showcase scs-056/057 ("What ships next") still narrates W2/W3 as future and contradicts its own scs-059 W3-amendment three blocks earlier. Checked-in scaffy/showcase/*.json payloads are byte-identical to the live papers — the D18 re-ingest recipe reproduces live state exactly; edit in place, re-POST.

(11) W3 residue: all 5 W3 PRs are MERGED (gh-verified #3743/#3745/#3748/#3754/#3755; ledger tasks done) and the engine was live-proven during survey (validate clean on 7/7, validate --repo anchors_ok:9, run --dry-run refuses bad vars exit 2 and writes zero bytes). The charter's W3 wave log claiming 4-of-5 stalled is STALE — Review owes the correction stamp. 8 backlog tasks open, none blocks W4 (two adjacencies: add-schema-type is a CORPUS command, NOT W4's doctype — do not conflate; elixir-local-gate-proof is load-bearing for slice 1's gate). No pre-filed W4 tasks — clean slate. Go builds need CC=/usr/bin/clang.

Coverage map — where surveyors looked, and what was NOT there

Checked and found: plugin law + bulldocs/tasks/tickets exemplars; schema-v2 field inventory + paper.json tags shape; visibility enforcement (query_controller, public_read plug); capabilities.ex manifest entries for doc.*; run.go flag parsing + table renderer; scaffy engine AST/parse/apply/receipt/repocheck; TestScaffyPureLocal mechanics; paper_cmd/cli.go dispatch; Studio editor shell + FieldInputs; tmux-console/--yes/mcp-curated trust precedents; corpus headers (7/7); live guerrilla (papers+tasks in Default/production, NO command schema yet — expected); both papers' live bodies vs checked-in payloads; W3 merge state via gh + ledger + live CLI runs.

Checked and NOT found (absences = decisions-in-waiting): no reusable weighted-tags schema type (hand-copy is the pattern); no "code"/syntax field type in Studio; no generic repo-files→server-documents seeding command anywhere (bp seed fabricates random data; mix-task seeders are server-side; Sync/github plugin are bidirectional overkill); no sandboxing substrate; no existing "enumerate N shell lines then consent" prompt shape — W4 introduces a new confirmation shape; docs/cards/cli.md documents neither the --yes convention nor resolveContext; docs/cards/studio.md doesn't cover the generic field renderer; no schemas array in tickets' manifest (code-built schema variant exists as a second pattern).

Corners no surveyor reached: the JS SDK surface (no W4 exposure claimed, but unchecked); TUI rendering of a command doc (generic desk assumed); api/test coverage of the createOrReplace mutation path and whether generic mutate validates content against the schema (verify closes this); Barkpark's own papers/tasks prior art — most surveyors used the wrong search form (bp search <terms> errors; the real form bp search query "…" -o json works, proven by the trust-precedents scout) — verify re-runs the sweep.

Verify plan — 7 assignments in flight

V1 elixir-ground-proof (opus, RUNS): prove a targeted single-file plugin test runs locally (CC=/usr/bin/clang mix test test/barkpark/plugins/<file>) — slice 1's gate viability; run the existing createOrReplace/mutations tests; read Content.Mutations for any schema-validation hook and any length cap on large text fields (does a 15KB multi-line string survive intact?). Verdict shapes slice 1's gate line and the seeding-mechanism fork.

V2 create-or-replace --file repro (sonnet, RUNS): bp doc create-or-replace paper --set _id=probe --file x.json --dry-run must error "unknown flag --file" (exact string + exit code); bp doc create --file --dry-run must preview cleanly. Nails the bug the seeding fork hinges on, zero server writes.

V3 studio source rendering (opus, RUNS): prove readonly_json's output on a bare multi-line string (mix run --no-start probe replicating the helper) — readable multi-line monospace vs JSON-escaped one-liner; recommend the source field type (text vs object vs one tiny FieldInputs clause) with the exact diff the Studio slice needs.

V4 dry-run as consent surface (opus, RUNS): build bp (CC=/usr/bin/clang) and run scaffy run <corpus cmd> --dry-run; inspect the asserts JSON — are CMD asserts enumerated with vars SUBSTITUTED and TIER ci marked deferred? If yes, pull's consent gate can reuse dry-run enumeration verbatim. Also inventory internal/scaffy's EXPORTED surface (Parse, validate entry, RunOptions) that scaffy_remote_cmd.go can call without touching the engine.

V5 go gate baseline (sonnet, RUNS): CC=/usr/bin/clang go build ./... && go vet ./internal/cli/... && go test ./internal/cli/... on main — proves builders inherit a green baseline incl. TestScaffyPureLocal.

V6 live read path (sonnet, RUNS): curl guerrilla /v1/data/query/production/paper with NO auth header (proves tokenless public read = the one-connect claim); curl a private type tokenless expecting 404; bp doc query paper --fields title --order title:asc -o table proves the fields/order/table path the catalog rides.

V7 prior-art + dup sweep (sonnet, RUNS): bp search query "…" -o json (the correct form) over scaffy/provenance/command-content topics; gh pr list --state open for scaffy branches and foreign claims on epic children — the concurrent-session dup law before Decide files tasks.

Verify — what the deep round proved (6 verifiers, 2026-07-16)

elixir-ground-proof: targeted single-file plugin mix test runs LOCALLY — media_test.exs → "3 tests, 0 failures" in 9.0s wall; slice gates can be local mix test lines, refuting the backlog worry (task closed at Decide). createOrReplace is green on main (pusher+backfill 42 tests, mutate_controller 12 tests, 0 failures). POST /v1/data/mutate performs ZERO schema-field validation: validate_document has exactly two callers repo-wide, both UI (forms.ex:242, studio doc.ex:21) — so the seeding fork is NOT differentiated by validation; the seeder owns correctness. content is jsonb with no practical cap; title is varchar(255) — the source must ride in content, never title.

create-or-replace-file-repro: the --file gap is REAL at runtime, not a manifest-reading artifact — `bp doc create-or-replace paper --file x.json --dry-run` fails exit 2 with "bp: unknown flag --file for doc create-or-replace" BEFORE any network call, because capabilities.ex:807-829 declares only flag("set") while the generic Writes help line (usage.go:144-151) advertises --file for every write verb. doc.create (:796) and doc.mutate (:710) are working controls; create-if-not-exists carries the identical gap. One-line-class fix — does not justify forking to a bespoke ingest endpoint.

studio-source-rendering: readonly_json on a bare multi-line .scaffy source emits a ONE-LINE JSON-escaped blob (proof: "# add-block-type v1\nCONCEPT add-block-type…" — every newline \n, every quote \\") — the array/object clause is disqualified for the source field. type "text" is readable but EDITABLE + form-submitted (a Studio save silently diverges server from repo). The winning shape: a new ~9-line FieldInputs clause for a fresh field type — read-only monospace <pre>, RAW value, NO form input (absent from params ⇒ Classic save preserves bytes byte-identical, forms.ex:168-181 precedent).

dry-run-as-consent-surface: `bp scaffy run --dry-run` ALREADY enumerates the substituted CMD surface — RunReport.Asserts[] carries the real var-woven shell text (proof: "echo checking widget && grep -q widget probe_widget.txt", status would-run), TIER ci CMDs come back status deferred ("TIER ci — deferred to the PR, never run locally"), and dry-run writes NOTHING. The consent gate is a REUSE, not an invention. Nuances that bind the design: injection commands abort at the op stage on anchor mismatch (distinct UX path, no CMD list); ValidateFile takes bytes (pre-write gate for fetched content); the substituter is unexported — enumeration is reachable ONLY through Run's dry-run; only 3 of 7 corpus commands have LOCAL would-run CMDs (4 are ci-only — say "no local commands run" honestly).

go-gate-baseline + live-read-path: main is GREEN (CC=/usr/bin/clang go build ./..., vet, full internal/cli suite ok in 36s; TestScaffyPureLocal and TestCompletionNounsCoverAllDispatchedBuiltins PASS by name); the cc-alias trap reconfirmed (without CC= the wrapper reds vet with "unknown option -E"). Live on guerrilla: tokenless GET of a public type returns 200 with documents; a private type 404s existence-hiding ("document not found") — visibility:"public" on the command schema IS the one-connect story. bp doc query --fields/--order renders a correctly projected+sorted table (zero new API for the catalog); caveat: columns empty across the whole page are dropped from the header (backlogged).

prior-art-dup-sweep: CLEAN — zero open PRs touch scaffy (all 17 scaffy PRs MERGED); all 8 open epic children unclaimed (claim:null); no scaffy plugin exists in api/lib (the W4 plugin is genuinely new); scaffy-backlog-add-schema-type confirmed DISTINCT (a deferred corpus command wrapping bp make schema — not W4's doctype). The charter's W3 wave log ("4 of 5 stalled") confirmed STALE against gh + ledger (all merged/done) — reconciled at Decide as D52. Coverage not-founds worth keeping: no capabilities_test.exs (the manifest gate is cli_commands_manifest_test.exs), no code/source field type anywhere, no reusable weighted-tags type, no existing pull-drift check.

Decide — D44–D53 (the charter is canonical; one-line mirrors here)

D44 — a NEW scaffy plugin owns the command schema (plugin-declared house law; bulldocs.ex:141-158 is the template); capabilities ["schemas"] only, visibility "public" — tokenless pull/ls proven live. D45 — the .scaffy source VERBATIM in ONE content string field typed "source": a new read-only monospace verbatim FieldInputs clause (readonly_json escapes, text is editable — both disqualified by proof); tags = arrayOf composite{tag,strength,rationale} copied from paper.json. D46 — stable id <domain>--<concept>--<variant> (concept alone non-unique); ALL metadata derived at seed time via scaffy.Parse — never hand-maintained twice.

D47 — seeding = bp doc create-or-replace command --file + bp doc publish, after adding flag("file") to create-or-replace AND create-if-not-exists; NO bespoke ingest endpoint (neither path validates — the fork buys nothing); seeder = go run ./scaffy/seed parsing the corpus via internal/scaffy; idempotent by _id (wholesale upsert). D48 — verbs are bp scaffy pull <concept>[/<variant>] + bp scaffy ls --remote, ALL remote code in NEW internal/cli/scaffy_remote_cmd.go (TestScaffyPureLocal substring-scan law; dispatch cases only in scaffy_cmd.go); bp add deferred to backlog as a future thin alias, never a second implementation.

D49 — trust model: pull NEVER runs anything; ValidateFile(fetched bytes) BEFORE any write (finding ⇒ exit 5, nothing on disk); pulled file byte-identical + a COMMITTED provenance sidecar next to it (never under .scaffy/ — that dir is gitignored receipts); running a sidecar-marked file dry-runs first, prints the SUBSTITUTED would-run CMDs + deferred count, then requires --yes or TTY confirm (non-TTY without --yes = exit 2); repo-authored files unchanged; no sandbox pretense — validate + enumerate + consent + provenance IS the model. D50 — catalog: ZERO new API (generic query + existing table renderer; Studio = editor shell + the one clause; no new LiveView). D51 — papers: masterplan gains one "commands are served now" paragraph after scf-055 (scf-033's bp add mock stays vision language); showcase scs-056/057 rewritten past-tense resolving the scs-059 contradiction, with REAL transcripts; D18 re-POST mechanism. D52 — W3 wave log reconciled: 5/5 merged (#3743/#3745/#3748/#3754/#3755). D53 — three sequenced rounds; dependents filed open with AFTER-X-merges stop-guards; the lead runs rounds 2–3 manually.

Wave plan — 5 slices, 3 rounds (in flight)

ROUND 1 (dispatch now, parallel, disjoint files): scaffy-w4-command-schema-plugin (opus; api/priv/plugins/scaffy/ + plugins/scaffy.ex + field_inputs.ex source clause; gate: cd api && CC=/usr/bin/clang mix test test/barkpark/plugins/scaffy_test.exs) ∥ scaffy-w4-file-flag-fix (opus; capabilities.ex flag("file") on create-or-replace + create-if-not-exists + protective test; gate: cd api && CC=/usr/bin/clang mix test test/barkpark/plugins/cli_commands_manifest_test.exs — green in 2s pre-change) ∥ scaffy-w4-pull-trust-cli (fable; internal/cli/scaffy_remote_cmd.go new + test + scaffy_cmd.go dispatch only; gate: CC=/usr/bin/clang go build ./... && go vet ./internal/cli/... && go test ./internal/cli/... -count=1).

ROUND 2 — scaffy-w4-seed-corpus (opus; scaffy/seed/; live gate: tokenless query count 7 + sha256 source parity ×7 + idempotent re-run) AFTER both round-1 Elixir slices merge (merged = auto-deployed). ROUND 3 — scaffy-w4-live-proof-papers-stamp (fable; scaffy/showcase/; live ls --remote table, pull→validate→sidecar→consent transcripts, papers re-POST 200, epic W4 criterion stamped) AFTER seed-corpus + pull-trust-cli merge. Both dependents are FILED OPEN with AFTER-X-merges stop-guard first lines (D43/D53 — the dispatcher runs ONLY round 1; manual sequential rounds went 4-for-4 in W3).

Backlog filed this wave: scaffy-backlog-bp-add-alias (p3, thin-alias decide-or-retire), scaffy-backlog-file-flag-sweep (p3, help-vs-manifest honesty across all write verbs), scaffy-backlog-pull-drift-check (p2, provenance drift R-004), scaffy-backlog-table-sparse-columns (p3, catalog UX nits). Closed at Decide: scaffy-backlog-elixir-local-gate-proof — A2's open half resolved LOCAL-safe-with-warm-_build, charter + README gate table updated (commit e9c1c022e).

Review — the debrief (2026-07-16)

What shipped (round 1, all three gates re-run green on the reviewer's own worktree; the lead merges these branches and closes each task's merge-gated criterion):

1. scaffy-w4-command-schema-plugin — merge loop-epic/command-doctype-live-new-scaffy-plugin-r-0-r (review branch). The command doctype via a NEW schemas-only scaffy plugin: plugin.json (capabilities ["schemas"]), command.json (visibility public; source typed "source" carrying the verbatim .scaffy bytes; concept/variant/domain/direction plain strings; weighted composite tags hand-copied from paper.json), scaffy.ex register_schemas/1 mirroring bulldocs.ex:141-158 verbatim, and the FieldInputs "source" clause: read-only monospace <pre>, raw multi-line value HTML-escaped, NO form input so a Classic save preserves bytes. Verdict: exemplary house-pattern work. Review verified LIVE that guerrilla runs discover-all plugin mode (no BARKPARK_PLUGINS whitelist in .env or systemd) — the plugin auto-registers on deploy, which is the exact fact the seed slice depends on. Review added render-level tests (the builder's one stated blind spot): the clause renders escaped multi-line source verbatim and emits no doc[...] input — 33 field_inputs tests green.

2. scaffy-w4-file-flag-fix — merge loop-epic/bp-doc-create-or-replace-create-if-not-e-1 (original branch — clean at review, nothing to fix). flag("file", ...) added to doc.create-or-replace AND doc.create-if-not-exists as a verbatim mirror of doc.create:796, plus a protective test looping both verbs (file-typed, non-repeatable, --set survives alongside). Gate re-run: 15 tests, 0 failures; mix format clean. Smallest possible diff for the proven live bug — exactly what the brief asked.

3. scaffy-w4-pull-trust-cli — merge loop-epic/bp-scaffy-pull-ls-remote-fetch-validate--2-r (the review branch, NOT the original). All remote code in the new scaffy_remote_cmd.go (TestScaffyPureLocal green — scaffy_cmd.go carries dispatch only); pull = fetch → ValidateFile BEFORE any write (exit 5, nothing written — proven by a ReadDir-empty test) → byte-identical .scaffy + committed .provenance.json sidecar (10-field struct equality pinned) → unsubstituted CMD templates + dry-run hint; ambiguous concept lists variants exit 2; ls --remote via the generic query endpoint through the existing table renderer. The D49 consent gate dry-runs first, prints substituted would-run vs deferred TIER-ci CMDs separately (honest "no local commands run" for ci-only), then --yes or TTY confirm; non-TTY refusal exit 2 mutates nothing. Review verified the REAL query envelope live against guerrilla (result-wrapped, content fields flat — both unmarshal paths in the code are needed and covered). REVIEW FIX (one real defect): under -o json the consent gate wrote prose to stdout and its refusal emitted no envelope, breaking the CLI's machine-parity convention — machine mode is now envelope-only ({ok:false, error.code:consent_required, would_run_cmds, deferred_cmds}; --yes passes the gate silently so the run's own envelope is the only stdout), pinned by a new two-case test. Plus a gofmt sweep of pre-existing drift in scaffy_cmd_test.go. Full gate spine (build + vet + internal/cli -count=1) green on the final state.

What stalled, honestly: scaffy-w4-seed-corpus (never claimed — its dependency, the command schema, cannot be on guerrilla until slice 1 merges and auto-deploys; the dispatched checker proved the absence live: /api/schemas has no command, the query 404s) and scaffy-w4-live-proof-papers-stamp (builder obeyed the brief's stop-guard, stamped nothing, faked nothing; review released the dead claim — task back to open). This is D53 working as designed: the dispatcher ran ONLY round 1, and both round-2/3 briefs are intact and ready for the manual sequential re-dispatch that went 4-for-4 in W3.

Ledger audit: clean — no fixes needed beyond the claim release. All three built slices sat in_progress with evidence stamped as work happened (now-lines told the story mid-flight), merge-gated criteria correctly left open for the lead; the two stalled tasks read exactly as stalled. One process note from the schema-plugin builder worth keeping: bp task stamp rejects a retyped em-dash in --criterion-text (byte-match is the contract) — fetch the stored wording programmatically and pass it verbatim.

Grade: A-. Strong: three slices that each do exactly their brief with the house pattern as law — the plugin is a faithful bulldocs mirror, the manifest fix is surgical, and the pull/trust surface is genuinely well-tested (16 mocked tests covering refusal-writes-nothing, byte-identity, substitution proof, W3-behavior regression). The trust model shipped as decided: validate-first + enumerate + consent + provenance, no sandbox pretense. Short of A: the wave planned 5 slices and landed 3 (by design, but the wish's endgame — commands actually SERVED and pulled from guerrilla — is still two merges + two re-dispatches away); the -o json consent defect shipped past a builder who had even flagged it himself rather than fixing it; ls --remote's single-page read is a small known debt. Nothing here is bloat — every line serves the wish.

Next: (1) lead merges the three branches (Elixir slices wait for the Elixir Test lane; PR bodies carry Task: lines), confirms guerrilla auto-deploy registers command (curl /api/schemas | grep command) and runs make cli-build; (2) re-dispatch seed-corpus; (3) after seed + pull merge, re-dispatch live-proof-papers-stamp (real transcripts, D51 papers re-POST, epic W4 criterion stamp). That closes the epic's last open criterion.
